questions.prompt: Cal is brash, blunt, and uses short sentences. Iris is careful, picks her words slowly, and uses long sentences with side-thoughts. Which line sounds like Iris?

options.label: "I think — and you can disagree with this — that maybe we both said too much."

questions.mentorPostScript: Iris uses commas, hedges, and self-correction. That's her fingerprint.

questions.prompt: A character's voice register tells you their stance + status + age + mood. Which of these tells you the MOST about a character?

options.label: How many exclamation points they use.
What they don't say — the words they avoid + the topics they sidestep.
Whether their name starts with a vowel.

questions.mentorPostScript: Voice is shaped by silence as much as speech.

questions.prompt: You write a line for the mentor character. The mentor is supposed to coach, not lecture. Which line stays in character?

options.label: "Let me explain why you are wrong."
"What did you notice when you said that?"

questions.mentorPostScript: The mentor asks. The mentor doesn't tell. That's the register.

questions.prompt: Two characters argue about the same thing — say, whether to leave the party early. They have different stakes. Which detail tells you the stakes are different?

options.label: One character keeps asking what time it is; the other keeps asking who else is still here.
Both characters say "I want to leave."

questions.mentorPostScript: Different stakes = different details inside the same argument.

options.label: Characters can drift toward sounding like each other when you're writing fast.
All dialogue should sound the same.
Only the protagonist's voice needs to be distinct.

questions.mentorPostScript: The drift is the craft challenge. Catching it in revision is half the work.
